surface_mechanism_description: The TiO2 film growth on Ru substrates showed a long incubation period, which decreased with increasing TTIP pulse time. The growth rate transition from low to high values was observed when the films were grown at temperatures above 250°C, due to the structural change from amorphous/nanocrystalline to well-crystallized polycrystalline anatase phase.
evidence: The TiO2 film growth on a Ru substrate showed a rather long incubation period and the incubation period decreased with increasing Ti /H20851OCH/H20849CH3/H208502/H208524 pulse time, whereas the H2O pulse time had almost no influence on the incubation period. A growth rate transition, from low to high values, /H20849thickness 7-8 nm/H20850was observed when the films were grown at temperatures /H11022250°C, whereas the films grown at lower temperatures did not show the transition. The transition was due to the structural change of the film from an amorphous/nanocrystalline to the well-crystallized polycrystalline anatase phase.
